changes.before: Thread block of one launch owning one dynamic shared-memory allocation; the scope of __syncthreads()
changes.after: Thread block owning one dynamic shared-memory smem allocation and CTA-scoped tensor memory tmem; the scope of __syncthreads()

changes.before: Single instruction-executing lane; 32 threads form one warp and a thread arrives alone on a barrier
changes.after: Lane with thread-local register values; 32 threads form one warp; each thread arrives individually on a barrier

changes.before: One symmetric role of eight warps; overlap comes from the two-slot cp.async ring - chunk c+1 in flight during chunk c - and register-resident operands: 16 cached phase-1 A-fragment steps and the 64x512 FP32 accumulator. Costs ~208 registers/thread, 207,232 B smem, one CTA per SM
changes.after: One symmetric role of eight warps; overlap comes from the two-slot cp.async ring - chunk c+1 in flight during chunk c - and register-resident operands: 16 cached phase-1 A-fragment steps and the 64x512 FP32 accumulator. Costs 207,232 B smem

changes.before: 256 threads per CTA, one-CTA-per-SM launch bound; one 207,232-byte dynamic smem allocation (storage account plus 256-byte slack) against the 232,448-byte device max minus ~1 KiB static; ~208 registers per thread without spilling
changes.after: 256 threads per CTA with __launch_bounds__(256, 1); one 207,232-byte dynamic smem request including 256-byte slack, checked against the runtime device opt-in maximum

changes.before: The Tile_pipeline account and the register-resident fragment and accumulator design assume exactly this residency and budget; an over-budget launch is rejected at the check rather than silently mis-laid-out
changes.after: The shared-memory request must cover the Tile_pipeline storage layout; run_cfg checks it against the device opt-in limit before launch; the registered arrays do not establish compiled register allocation or spilling

changes.before: A separate 32,768-byte query tile would need 235,456 bytes against a 231,424-byte budget, so the tile trades it for 128 registers of cached A fragments per thread on top of 64 accumulator registers; the slot-0 release barrier is what makes the reuse safe
changes.after: A separate 32,768-byte query tile would need 235,456 bytes against a 231,424-byte layout budget; cached A fragments and accumulators instead hold 128 and 64 32-bit slots per thread, without determining compiled register allocation; the slot-0 release barrier makes reuse safe

changes.before: 512 threads per CTA under a two-blocks-per-SM launch bound, i.e. 64 registers per thread, a 9,776-byte static shared block and no dynamic shared memory; four segment-groups of 128 threads each own one float4 of the 512 latent columns
changes.after: 512 threads per CTA with __launch_bounds__(512, 2), a 9,776-byte static shared block and no dynamic shared memory; four segment-groups of 128 threads each own one float4 of the 512 latent columns

changes.before: The merge is bound by dependent-load latency rather than bandwidth, so its parallelism has to come from threads; the 64-register cap is what limits the prefetched quad depth to four, and only the first 128 threads own the merged output
changes.after: The merge hides dependent-load latency with four segment groups and four prefetched quads per thread; only the first 128 threads own the merged output, and the launch bound does not specify the compiled register count

changes.before: Lanes read their o columns from tmem_alloc in 32-column segments, multiply by inv, round to BF16 into the dead kv_ring staging at 1040-byte pitch
changes.after: Read o from tmem_alloc, scale by inv and round to BF16 into dead kv_ring at 1040-byte row pitch; 64 rows span both stages, reserved by out_block

changes.before: Gathered KV chunk rows; dead ring stages out_block
changes.after: Two gather stages; dead storage holds output

changes.before: Union chunk rows; dead stages hold build and out
changes.after: Two gather stages; dead allocation holds build/out
